articles.title: Privacy Act of 1974; Matching Program
articles.summary: In accordance with the Privacy Act of 1974, as amended, the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and the Social Security Administration (SSA) are providing notice of a new computer matching program. Under this program, SSA will disclose Social Security Number (SSN) verifications to the Federal Housing Administration (FHA) through HUD to verify Borrowers' eligibility to participate in FHA's Single Family mortgage insurance programs. The matching program will enable HUD to verify Social Security numbers and related identifying information submitted by individuals applying for FHA-insured mortgage programs.
articles.mortgageRelevance: FHA mortgage borrower eligibility verification and the HUD/SSA matching program.

articles.title: 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act Prohibition on Large Institutional Investor Purchases of Single-Family Homes
articles.summary: The Department of the Treasury (Treasury) is issuing this proposed rule to carry out the purposes of section 1001 of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (the Act or the ROAD Act). Section 1001 of the ROAD Act prohibits large institutional investors from purchasing single-family homes, subject to certain exceptions. The proposed rule would clarify certain terms relevant to those restrictions, including "large institutional investor"; clarify the application of certain exceptions from the statutory prohibition; and clarify the statutory enforcement mechanism. The proposed rule is intended to provide clarity to market participants and other stakeholders on the application of the statute before the effective date of the ROAD Act.
articles.mortgageRelevance: Proposed implementation of statutory restrictions on institutional purchases of single-family homes.

articles.title: Mortgage and Loan Insurance Programs Under the National Housing Act-Debenture Interest Rates
articles.summary: This Notice announces changes in the interest rates to be paid on debentures issued with respect to a loan or mortgage insured by the Federal Housing Administration under the provisions of the National Housing Act (the Act). The interest rate for debentures issued under Section 221(g)(4) of the Act during the 6-month period beginning July 1, 2026, is 4\1/2\ percent. The interest rate for debentures issued under any other provision of the Act is the rate in effect on the date that the commitment to insure the loan or mortgage was issued, or the date that the loan or mortgage was endorsed (or initially endorsed if there are two or more endorsements) for insurance, whichever rate is higher. The interest rate for debentures issued under these other provisions with respect to a loan or mortgage committed or endorsed during the 6-month period beginning July 1, 2026, is 5 percent.
articles.mortgageRelevance: HUD statutory FHA mortgage-insurance debenture rate notice, not a weekly market-rate survey.

articles.title: Section 184 Indian Housing Loan Guarantee Program Increase in the Loan Guarantee Fee
articles.summary: The Section 184 Indian Housing Loan Guarantee Program ("Section 184 Program") operates using a combination of funds annually appropriated by Congress and fees. Consistent with other HUD loan guarantee programs, to ensure that the program is self-sustaining, HUD is increasing fees charged under the program. HUD is increasing the upfront loan guarantee fee for all new Section 184 Firm Commitments, including refinances, from 1.00 to 1.50 percent, effective October 1, 2026. HUD is increasing the upfront loan guarantee fee for all new Section 184 Skilled Workers Demonstration Program Firm Commitments, from 0 to 1.00 percent, effective October 1, 2026. The Annual Loan Guarantee Fee will remain at zero for all Section 184 loans.
articles.mortgageRelevance: Increase in Section 184 housing loan guarantee fees for new firm commitments.
